AR Emerging awards 2026 winners revealed

15 October 2026 By AR Editors AR Emerging Reading Time: 3 minutes

Share
Comment
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 2:39
Instaread

Atelier Julien Boidot have been announced as the winner of the AR Emerging awards 2026, along with Rodríguez + De Mitri who have been highly commended, and A-A Collective who have won the Peter Davey Prize

School complex in Valmondois, France by Atelier Julien Boidot

Credit: Clément Guillaume

Atelier Julien Boidot have been named the winner of the 2026 AR Emerging awards, receiving a £5,000 prize. Selected from a shortlist of 10 young practices, the studio was chosen by an esteemed panel of judges, comprising Hanif Kara, co-founder of AKT II; Oliver Wainwright, architecture and design critic at the Guardian; and Christelle Avenier, co-founder of Avenier Cornejo and winner of the AR Emerging awards 2017.

Profiles of all this year’s shortlisted practices have been published in AR October 2026: click here to buy a copy

The judges highlighted that Atelier Julien Boidot was ‘a savvy model for practice’, with a team including a quantity surveyor, engineer and interior designer in house. With a focus on educational typologies, the work of Atelier Julien Boidot has increased urgency at a time when the quality of schools in France is under scrutiny. ‘The architecture possesses a confidence and requires no explanation,’ the judges explain.

House in Cuernavaca, Mexico by Rodriguez + De Mitri

Credit: César Béjar

Rodríguez + De Mitri were highly commended by the jury for asking ‘how much or how little needs to be built’ and ‘building with an economy of means’. The Sian Ka’an reforestation nursery ‘understands the forest and touches it lightly’, working ‘intelligently with material’.

The redesign of Warsaw’s central square, Plac Defilad, is A-A Collective’s first built project

Credit: Jędrzej Sokołowski

A-A Collective have been awarded this year’s Peter Davey Prize – a prize presented to the editors’ choice. ‘Warsaw Central Square is one of the best new public spaces in Europe,’ explains Manon Mollard, editor of  The Architectural Review. ‘A-A Collective have strengthened and celebrated public space at a time when it is in increasingly under threat.’ Working itinerantly across Switzerland, Denmark and Italy, the collective ‘offers an experimental model for practice that overcomes the common barriers to emerging practitioners.’

Each practice shortlisted for this year’s awards received a small token, crafted from different colour mixes

Credit: Josh Linnemann

The winners of the awards, announced today (Thursday 15 October) at the Architectural Association in London, received a trophy made of 90 per cent construction and demolition waste, designed by low-carbon brick manufacturer Kenoteq.

First launched in 1999, the AR Emerging awards grant early recognition to young designers and celebrate the architectural stars of tomorrow. Since 2018, the awards have recognised a body of work rather than a single building, and aspiring candidates share a small portfolio of three projects with us: a completed building, a work in progress and an idea. Early winners include Boonserm Premthada, Thomas Heatherwick and Frida Escobedo; more recent winners and commended include ARB Architects, Material Cultures and Pihlmann Architects.
